summary.headline: Emcure Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR2,820 crore, and management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to above 20% from mid-teens.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR2,820 crore, up 24.3% YoY and 9.3% QoQ, with growth across India, Europe, Canada and Rest of World. EBITDA rose 31% to INR575 crore at a 20.4% margin, about 100 bps higher YoY, and PAT rose 29% to INR325 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to above 20% and now expects the EBITDA margin gain at the upper end of the 75-100 bps range. Net debt rose to INR1,317 crore after INR551 crore of acquisition-related payouts in H1, and the company remains committed to net cash by end FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +31% YoY; margin +~100 bps YoY, +~70 bps QoQ
vs INR39 crore last year, lower FX gains
higher on borrowings for acquisition payouts

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,155 crore, up 12% YoY; organic growth 10% vs 6% in Q1. Zuventus is about 25% of group revenue and improved QoQ; management guides India to around low-teens growth for FY27.

segments.name: Europe (incl. UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR604 crore, up 36% YoY, driven by base portfolio, new launches and liposomal amphotericin B. Treprostinil flagged as the next significant contributor.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR431 crore, up 24% YoY, driven by base business and recent launches; further launches expected in H2.

segments.name: Rest of World (emerging markets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR630 crore, up 41% YoY. ARV and non-ARV both grew; ARV was about half of RoW sales in Q2 versus about 65% in Q1.

segments.name: International total
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,665 crore, up 34.5% YoY, 59% of group revenue; about 10 pts of currency benefit, constant-currency international growth about 24%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected to exceed 20%, versus mid-teens guided earlier.
FY27 EBITDA margin expansion now expected at the upper end of the 75-100 bps guidance range.
India expected to grow about low-teens for FY27, with exit-FY27 growth at or above industry.
R&D to step up in H2 but remain within 4-5% of revenue for FY27; H1 R&D was INR111 crore, about 4% of revenue.
FY27 RoW ARV share expected around 50-55%.
Committed to becoming net cash by end of FY28; no FY28 numeric guidance given.
Margin gains expected mainly from operating leverage, with SG&A growing slower than revenue; no meaningful opex step-ups flagged.
capex_capacity: MR headcount steady at about 4,100-4,200; no near-term additions planned.

Amphotericin B produced at two manufacturing sites, each serving specific markets; recent regulatory audits closed, and management expects facilities to serve without restriction in the next 18-24 months.
Amphotericin B batches already under production for newly approved markets; launches in at least a couple of market buckets over the next half.

Approvals received in the quarter (over 20 in total) include liposomal amphotericin B in Brazil and Mexico and bevacizumab for wet AMD in India; lenacapavir PrEP got a positive SEC recommendation in India.
Lenacapavir dossiers filed with WHO and US FDA for RoW markets; reviews expected over the next few quarters.
Semaglutide filing in Canada expected in the next few months; Quebec semaglutide launch with Dr. Reddy's depends on supply timing (partner has indicated November).
demand_pricing: Domestic IPM growth has picked up over the last 3-4 quarters, which management attributes to healthcare access, demand for quality branded generics, and GLP-1 related diagnostics; obesity is estimated at 4-5% of a roughly INR25,000 crore market.
Poviztra (Novo Nordisk partnership, obesity) was number 4 brand on IQVIA last month and expected to improve by at least one rank in October.

Europe: treprostinil described as a high-value, limited-competition product, expected to contribute significantly. Amphotericin B penetration in Europe is about 50% with around 20 countries still to enter.
Amphotericin B is well below 10% of international sales, per management; Europe may face competition over time.
In-licensed products are about high-teens % of India sales; biosimilars about 10% of India sales.
Raw material: imported input costs and freight/insurance costs rose; currency gains offset most of this, keeping gross margin impact muted.
Zuventus: recovery from H2 FY26 attrition; management expects H2 FY27 to be strong versus H2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much does amphotericin B contribute to Europe, and what other product could add in the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not break out by product; it is a key driver but not the only one. Treprostinil is the next product expected to contribute significantly in Europe, with limited competition and strong value and margin.

qa_highlights.question: How long for Zuventus and organic domestic growth to reach industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 FY27 to be strong versus H2 FY26 for Zuventus, and expects overall growth to be broadly in line with the IPM by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the constant-currency growth?
qa_highlights.answer: International currency impact about 10 pts. Constant-currency international growth about 24%; overall growth about 18.5% in constant currency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India profitability hierarchy and ARV visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: India is the number one profitability vertical, though in-licensed business is lower margin. Europe, Canada and RoW non-ARV are strongly profitable; ARV margins are below corporate average. R&D is tilted to international. Lenacapavir is expected to be margin accretive over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RoW ARV vs non-ARV split?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly half of RoW sales in Q2 were ARV, versus about 65-67% in Q1. Management expects FY27 ARV at about 50-55% of RoW.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex grow faster than revenue, and what is the MR plan?
qa_highlights.answer: No meaningful opex step-ups flagged; SG&A to grow slower than revenue. MR count stays at about 4,100-4,200 with no additions; productivity per rep rose QoQ.

risks_watch: Zuventus recovery must hold through H2 FY27 to bring domestic growth to industry levels; the company does not disclose Zuventus growth separately.
Europe amphotericin B competition expected at some point; mitigated by two manufacturing sites, but site-specific approvals still pending.
Raw material and freight cost inflation; management cited geopolitical risk (Iran conflict, oil prices) as a swing factor for growth outlook.
Net debt up INR263 crore in H1 after acquisition payouts; net cash target by end FY28 depends on cash generation.
Pending NCLT approval for the amalgamation of Zuventus Healthcare and Emcutix Biopharmaceuticals into Emcure.
Lenacapavir and semaglutide (Canada filing, Quebec launch) timing depends on regulatory reviews and supply.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the raised FY27 guidance, with broad-based growth cited. Management was more cautious on India/Zuventus timing and on FY28, declining to give numeric FY28 guidance and refusing to break out OTC, Zuventus and product-level figures.
key_quotes: We now expect revenue growth to exceed 20% compared to mid-teens mentioned earlier.
EBITDA margin improvement for the year is now expected to be at the upper end of our guidance range of 75 to 100 basis points.
So, if you are growing at 8%, 12% is granted, it is going to happen, 11%, 12%.
It's not really going to happen in a day, but we obviously see ourselves a long-term player in this particular market and things are happening in the right direction.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to above 20% from mid-teens, backed by H1 revenue up 23.6% YoY, international growth of 34.5%, new launches (liposomal amphotericin B, treprostinil next) and margin gains from operating leverage, though no specific capacity additions were quantified.
